title: Ops priority flip — internal comms + Q&A scratch
content:
Purpose: quick internal briefing and working Q&A for the ops priority flip announcement. This is a scratchpad — rough, short bullets, things to test in soundcheck.

Context (one-liner):
- We are shifting short-term engineering and infra effort to prioritize capacity and reliability actions tied to peak region demand (priority flip). This is a 6–8 week focused window with targeted mitigations and temporary feature gating.

Audience: engineering teams, product owners, platform SREs, and leadership. Tone: direct, practical, low-fear, clear tradeoffs.

Slack announcement (short, single-paragraph):
- TL;DR: Starting next Monday we'll run a 6–8 week ops priority window to reduce regional latency and reduce cold-start failures. We'll temporarily delay low-priority feature rollouts and reorient certain backlog items to reliability work. Expect updates in #ops-announce and a weekly status note from the platform team.

All-hands 3-minute script (tight):
- Opening (15s): Hi — quick update: we’re flipping short-term priorities to focus on reliability and capacity in a few regions.
- Why (30s): Over the last quarter, we've seen correlated increases in tail latency during peak windows in EU-W and APAC staging; this is impacting SLAs and some customer deployments.
- What (60s): For ~6–8 weeks we will: 1) pause non-critical feature merges into main for affected services, 2) prioritize autoscaling and cache tuning, 3) run targeted load tests and roll out optimized kernel profiles, and 4) offer dedicated support for customers on Dedicated/Private who flag incidents.
- Impact/what to expect (45s): Developers — short-lived PR freezes on selected services (you’ll get a list/day-by-day); PMs — some roadmap items will be scoped now vs later; Sales/CS — priority incident handling remains but we’ll proactively reach out if a customer is at risk.
- Close (20s): This is temporary, measurable, and reversible. We’ll report weekly with metrics and rollback criteria. Thanks to the Platform and SRE squads for leading.

Anticipated questions + suggested answers (soundbites):
- Q: Is this a hiring freeze?
  A: No. This is a temporary shift of current sprint capacity and contractor focus, not a hiring change.
- Q: Which services are affected?
  A: Services that serve inference routing, runtime batching, and the autoscaler are in scope. We’ll publish an exact list by EOD Friday.
- Q: Will customers notice feature delays?
  A: Maybe for a small set of non-critical features; we’ll ask PMs to surface any customer commitments and work to mitigate.
- Q: How will we measure success?
  A: Reduce 95th/99th latency in target regions by X% (metric to be finalized), lower cold-start rate by Y, and maintain request throughput targets. Weekly dashboard + post-mortem.
- Q: Can teams opt out?
  A: Teams with critical launches tied to ARR or compliance can request exemptions via the escalation form; leadership will review.

Approval checklist (quick):
- [ ] Leadership brief completed (email to execs) — Rowan to send by Friday midday.
- [ ] Service list confirmed (platform owners) — Diego to compile by Thu.
- [ ] Slack + Confluence posts scheduled — Maya to publish on Monday 9am PT.
- [ ] Weekly dashboard created (observability team) — link included in confluence.
- [ ] Support escalation template ready — Priya to confirm.

Escalation flow (notes-to-self):
- Triage in #ops-incident -> platform on-call -> PagerDuty severity -> Exec standby if customer-impacting (Rowan, Maya). Keep CS looped.

Internal comm cadence (proposed):
- Monday kick: Slack + Confluence + short email to execs.
- Weekly status: Friday digest (metrics, open items, wins).
- Mid-window review (week 4): public recap, decide continuation/rollback.

Things to test in soundcheck (observations):
- Read the slack announcement out loud — it must be <280 chars for headline.
- Pause after "this is temporary" to avoid alarm.
- Practice the metric placeholder — have concrete numbers ready or say 'we will publish targets by Wednesday'.

Draft Slack post (for Maya to edit):
- Heads-up: Starting Mon we’ll run a 6–8 week ops priority window to focus on regional reliability and capacity. We’ll pause low-priority merges for selected infra services, push targeted autoscaling/cache work, and run focused load tests. Watch #ops-announce for the service list and weekly updates. Reach out to @Rowan or @Maya for urgent questions.

Room for nuance / optional lines:
- Highlight that Dedicated/private customers flagged for risk will get a named contact and quicker SLAs during the window.
- Emphasize that feature parity for core APIs is not changing — this is about stability and predictability.

Open questions (still need to decide):
- Exact numeric targets for latency/cold-start reductions (obs team to propose).
- Which PM roadmaps will be pushed and how we'll compensate for schedule shifts.
- Default length (6 vs 8 weeks) — propose 6 weeks with a flexible extension based on metrics.

Notes-to-self (personal):
- Keep language simple. Avoid words like "freeze" in public messages — prefer "temporary pause".
- Get legal/infosec eyes only if any customer comms mention specific accounts.
- Prepare an FAQ doc (short) to post next to the confluence plan.

Next actions (immediate):
- Row 1: send leadership brief draft to execs by Fri 12:30pm (Rowan).
- Row 2: finalize affected service list (Diego) by Thu EOD.
- Row 3: schedule Monday slack/confluence post (Maya).
- Row 4: obs team to produce baseline metrics by Thu.

Version notes: rough scratch — will convert to polished confluence with tables and links once leaders ok the approach.

-- end scratch --
